Richard Partridge and Bob Treadwell had their own private battle for first. Partridge won on the day but was later disqualified as it was found that his residential qualification was not yet valid - so Oliver gained Silver - our best performance since Gerry North's days.

Marcello Bizio, finishing fifth overall, was runner up to Bob Treadwell in the Surrey Championship. 1, P.Evans (Belgrave) 62:13; 2, P.Ellis (Canada) 64:46; 3, V.Garner (Aldershot F&D) 66:11; ... 5, M.Bizio 70:01.
Then Jim Estall, unhappy with the cold, but finishing a fine 14th, again ahead of BVAF National Champion Barry Atwell and also Bob Treadwell.

At the front Bob Treadwell won his third Championship in 25:11 from Grenville Tuck, first M45 in a new record time of 25:37. First Belgravian home was Mike Nouch in 9th, running slightly slower than his best time in 26:50.

Left: It's November 26th 1977 at Parliament Hill and showing no fear, eighteen year-old Dave Beaver (253), racing in the classic Polytechnic Harriers singlet, locks horns with "Bootsie" Dave Bedford (284) in the London Cross Country Championships. Bedford won with Dave 4th and Bob Treadwell (329 in the photo) 2nd.
